title: HeavyLocker: Lock Heavy Hitters in Distributed Data Streams

problem.claim: Detecting heavy hitters in distributed data streams requires balancing performance with accuracy, especially when extending beyond local heavy hitter detection.

gap.claim: Most existing sketch algorithms target local heavy hitters in a single stream, while few support global heavy hitter detection across distributed streams.

contributions.claim: HeavyLocker is a sketch algorithm that uses the separability of heavy hitters to lock and protect potential heavy hitters during stream processing.
The locking mechanism supports both local and global heavy hitter detection.
The paper provides theoretical analysis of HeavyLocker's locking mechanism.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly introduce HeavyLocker as a novel sketch algorithm based on the separability of heavy hitters.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that theoretical analysis validates the efficacy of HeavyLocker's locking mechanism.
The authors report that extensive experiments show HeavyLocker outperforms five benchmarked algorithms in accuracy while maintaining fast speed for local and global detection.
The authors report that HeavyLocker reduces errors by up to an order of magnitude compared with Double-Anonymous Sketch.

narrative_sequence.summary: Sketching is used to identify heavy hitters in large-scale data streams.
Existing sketches are mainly designed for local detection, with limited support for global detection across distributed streams, and must balance accuracy with performance.
HeavyLocker exploits heavy hitter separability by locking and protecting potential heavy hitters during processing.
The locking capability enables application to global detection tasks.
The authors report theoretical validation and experimental improvements in accuracy, speed, and error reduction against benchmarks.

source_observation.claim: The method locks and protects potential heavy hitters by exploiting their separability.

interpretation.claim: Using a structural property of the target signal may improve the accuracy-speed tradeoff in streaming sketches.

application.claim: For distributed stream detection, consider preserving likely high-frequency items during processing when the data exhibits separable heavy hitters.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether the approach works when heavy hitters are not separable.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the formal definition or assumptions of heavy hitter separability.
The abstract does not provide datasets, workload settings, algorithmic complexity, or detailed benchmark results.
